23:     dataset_out : array-like, shape=(n_ts, original_size, d), dtype=float64
24:         A dataset of time series corresponding to the provided
25:         representation.
26:     """
27:     n_ts, sz, d = dataset_paa.shape
28:     seg_sz = original_size // sz
29:     dataset_out = np.zeros((n_ts, original_size, d))
30:     for t in prange(sz):
31:         t0 = t * seg_sz
32:         for i_ts in range(n_ts):
33:             dataset_out[i_ts, t0 : t0 + seg_sz, :] = dataset_paa[i_ts, t, :]
34:     return dataset_out
35: 
36: 
37: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
38: def cydist_sax(sax1, sax2, breakpoints, original_size):
39:     """Compute distance between SAX representations as defined in [1]_.
40: 
41:     Parameters
42:     ----------
43:     sax1 : array-like, shape=(sz, d)
44:         SAX representation of a time series.
45:     sax2 : array-like, shape=(sz, d)
46:         SAX representation of another time series.
47:     breakpoints : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
48:         The breakpoints used to assign the alphabet symbols.
49:     original_size : int64 (Linux and MacOS) or int32 (Windows)
50:         Length of the original time series.
51: 
52:     Returns
53:     -------
54:     dist_sax : float64
55:         SAX distance.
56: 
57:     References
58:     ----------
59:     .. [1] J. Lin, E. Keogh, L. Wei, et al. Experiencing SAX: a novel
60:        symbolic representation of time series.
61:        Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery, 2007. vol. 15(107)
62:     """
63:     assert sax1.shape == sax2.shape
64:     s = 0.0
65:     sz, d = sax1.shape
66:     for t in prange(sz):
67:         for di in range(d):
68:             if np.abs(sax1[t, di] - sax2[t, di]) > 1:
69:                 max_symbol = max(sax1[t, di], sax2[t, di])
70:                 min_symbol = min(sax1[t, di], sax2[t, di])
71:                 s += (breakpoints[max_symbol - 1] - breakpoints[min_symbol]) ** 2
72:     dist_sax = np.sqrt(s * float(original_size) / sz)
73: 
74:     return dist_sax
75: 
76: 
77: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
78: def inv_transform_sax(dataset_sax, breakpoints_middle_, original_size):
79:     """Compute time series corresponding to given SAX representations.
80: 
81:     Parameters
82:     ----------
83:     dataset_sax : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, d), dtype=float64 (Linux and MacOS) or float32 (Windows)
84:         A dataset of SAX series.
85:     breakpoints_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
86:     original_size : int64 (Linux and MacOS) or int32 (Windows)
87:         Length of the original time series.
88: 
89:     Returns
90:     -------
91:     dataset_out : array-like, shape=(n_ts, original_size, d), dtype=float64
92:     """
93:     n_ts, sz, d = dataset_sax.shape
94:     seg_sz = original_size // sz
95:     dataset_out = np.zeros((n_ts, original_size, d))
96: 
97:     for i in prange(n_ts):
98:         for t in range(sz):
99:             t0 = t * seg_sz
100:             dataset_out[i, t0 : t0 + seg_sz, :] = breakpoints_middle_[
101:                 dataset_sax[i, t, :]
102:             ]
103:     return dataset_out
104: 
105: 
106: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
107: def cyslopes(dataset, t0):
108:     """Compute slopes.
109: 
110:     Parameters
111:     ----------
112:     dataset : array-like, shape=(n_ts, sz, d), dtype=float64
113:     t0 : int32
114: 
115:     Returns
116:     -------
117:     dataset_out : array-like, shape=(n_ts, d), dtype=float64
118:     """
119:     n_ts, sz, d = dataset.shape
120:     dataset_out = np.empty((n_ts, d))
121:     vec_t = np.arange(t0, t0 + sz).reshape((-1, 1))
122:     for i in prange(n_ts):
123:         for di in range(d):
124:             with objmode(dataset_out_i_di="float64"):
125:                 dataset_out_i_di = (
126:                     LinearRegression()
127:                     .fit(vec_t, dataset[i, :, di])
128:                     .coef_[0]
129:                 )
130:             dataset_out[i, di] = dataset_out_i_di
131:     return dataset_out
132: 
133: 
134: @njit(parallel=True, fastmath=True)
135: def cydist_1d_sax(
136:     sax1, sax2, breakpoints_avg_middle_, breakpoints_slope_middle_, original_size
137: ):
138:     """Compute distance between 1d-SAX representations as defined in [1]_.
139: 
140:     Parameters
141:     ----------
142:     sax1 : array-like, shape=(sz, 2 * d), dtype=float64 (Linux and MacOS) or float32 (Windows)
143:         1d-SAX representation of a time series.
144:     sax2 : array-like, shape=(sz, 2 * d), dtype=float64 (Linux and MacOS) or float32 (Windows)
145:         1d-SAX representation of another time series.
146:     breakpoints_avg_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
147:     breakpoints_slope_middle_ : array-like, ndim=1, dtype=float64
148:     original_size : int64 (Linux and MacOS) or int32 (Windows)
149:         Length of the original time series.
150: 
151:     Returns
152:     -------
153:     dist_1d_sax : float64
154:         1d-SAX distance.
155: 
156:     Notes
157:     -----
158:     Unlike SAX distance, 1d-SAX distance does not lower bound Euclidean
159:     distance between original time series.
160: 
161:     References
162:     ----------
163:     .. [1] S. Malinowski, T. Guyet, R. Quiniou, R. Tavenard. 1d-SAX: a
164:        Novel Symbolic Representation for Time Series. IDA 2013.
165:     """
166:     sz, d_1d_sax = sax1.shape
167:     assert sz == sax2.shape[0] and d_1d_sax == sax2.shape[1]
168:     s = 0.0
169:     d = d_1d_sax // 2
170:     seg_sz = original_size // sz
171: 
172:     for t in prange(sz):
173:         t0 = t * seg_sz
174:         t_middle = float(t0) + 0.5 * seg_sz
175:         for di in range(d):
176:             avg1 = breakpoints_avg_middle_[sax1[t, di]]
177:             avg2 = breakpoints_avg_middle_[sax2[t, di]]
178:             slope1 = breakpoints_slope_middle_[sax1[t, di + d]]
